persistence: Overall PR-AUC is 2.91× the base rate, but after a passing build it is 2.61× (ROC-AUC 0.743, moderate) and with no history 1.72× (ROC-AUC 0.724, moderate). Much of the score reflects the project's recent build outcomes (a broken build tends to stay broken) rather than the risk of the change itself.
ci_failure_not_outage: The label is a Travis CI build failing or erroring. It says nothing about production incidents, deployment regressions or user impact.
travis_transfer: Training data are open-source Java projects on Travis CI, 2011–2015. Modern CI (GitHub Actions), other languages, private codebases, monorepos and today's tooling may behave differently; performance on a tenant's repositories is unknown until measured on their history.
explanations: are SHAP attributions of the model's score, not causes of failure.
intended_use: Rank incoming builds / pull requests by risk of CI build failure, from historical patterns, at the moment the build is triggered, so reviewers can prioritise attention.
Shown next to (never instead of) the actual CI result.
Not for: predicting production outages or incidents, judging or ranking people, automatically blocking merges without human review, or any decision about an individual contributor.
